title: Do not sell public infrastructure with protections from competition
action: Review privatisation guidelines so that leases and sales of ports and other infrastructure do not include terms that restrict competition, such as limits on rival facilities, unless the benefits clearly outweigh the costs, and report on progress publicly.
why: Selling assets with restrictions that raise the sale price, such as bans on competing ports or high access charges, transfers costs to users for decades.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Procurement and privatisation policies and practices should not restrict competition unless: • the benefits of the restrictions to the community as a whole outweigh the costs; and • the objectives of the policy can only be achieved by restricting competition.
